title: SPI service descriptor (schema v3)
description: Fork-owned acceptance contract at .spi/service.yaml. Declares what a service's acceptance suite needs, symbolically: bindings from a closed source vocabulary resolved per run against the stack's facts envelope (spi info --json, apiVersion spi.osdu.dev/v1), Key Vault secret references (names, never values), required loads and entitlement groups, sibling dependencies, and a timeout. The resolver engine (.github/actions/acceptance-resolver) is the authority on enforcement; it additionally rejects reserved environment variable names (exact: AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID, AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE, and common process names such as PATH, HOME, LD_PRELOAD, MAVEN_OPTS; prefixes: ACTIONS_, GITHUB_, RUNNER_, SPI_STACK_) and any key outside this schema, exiting 2 with the offending key named.

schemaVersion.description: Contract version. Unknown versions are a hard failure; the vocabulary grows only by a template contract change.

archetype.description: Build/test archetype. Deliberately closed; new archetypes arrive by contract change.

tests.description: Named suites of one shape. An empty map declares a deploy-only lane: the image is borrowed, verified and restored with no suite. Otherwise acceptance is required and is the upstream <svc>-acceptance-test by default; a fork adds others, for example integration for its provider suite. The acceptance image bakes every declared suite path.

componentGovernance.description: Inputs of the Component Governance pipeline (.azuredevops/component-governance.yml, ADR-047), which registers what the fork ships and generates its NOTICE. Optional; the acceptance resolver validates it and does not read it.

upstream.description: The OSDU community project the fork is built from, without .git. Registered as the git component of the generated upstream commit.

image.description: GHCR package name of the service image, when the fork's SERVICE_NAME variable makes Validation publish it under a name other than the repository's. Default: the repository name. The loader image is <image>-load.

module.description: Repository-relative directory of the Spring Boot module the image ships. Default: the one module under provider/*-azure (one level deeper allowed) whose pom declares spring-boot-maven-plugin.

profiles.description: Maven profiles that build the module. Default: [core, azure] (ADR-035).

ignoreDirectories.description: Repository-relative directories Component Governance does not scan, such as Python test suites that ship in no image. Must not contain the module.

source.description: Closed source vocabulary. Facts: gateway (base_url), gatewayHost (the host and port of base_url, without scheme or path, for suites that build the URL themselves), partition (primary partition name), openid (OIDC v2.0 issuer URL, published explicitly by the stack), tenant (azure.tenant_id), legalTag (primary partition's legal_tag), domain (the entitlements domain the stack deployed, published as entitlements_domain). keyvault:<name> reads that secret from the stack's vault. forward:<target>:host and forward:<target>:port are where the suite reaches a target it declares in forwards: the host is localhost in the lane (the caller may name another, such as a container engine's host alias) and the port is the one the stack publishes. static carries the declared value; template renders ${NAME} references to other (non-template, non-secret) bindings after everything else resolves; user must be supplied by the caller's environment; token is the bearer the caller minted for this run, supplied as RESOLVER_TOKEN; memberToken is the bearer minted for the stack's member identity, a plain user with no admin rights, supplied as RESOLVER_MEMBER_TOKEN; noAccessToken is the bearer minted for the stack's no-access identity, supplied as RESOLVER_NO_ACCESS_TOKEN. Anything else is a hard failure naming the key.

suffix.description: Appended to a fact-sourced value (gateway values have their trailing slash stripped first). Fact sources only.

value.description: Required for static and template sources; invalid elsewhere.

default.description: Fallback when the fact or caller environment does not supply an answer. Invalid for keyvault, token, memberToken, and noAccessToken sources (a default secret would put a secret value in the repository), for forward sources, and for static/template.

type.description: maven runs the suite with Maven from its pom.xml. pytest runs python -m pytest in the suite directory with the declared requirements installed when the image is built.

path.description: Repository-relative working directory of the suite, e.g. the upstream <svc>-acceptance-test module.

mavenArguments.description: Individual Maven argv tokens. Consumers pass the decoded array directly to Maven and never evaluate it as a shell string. Maven suites only.

pytestArguments.description: Individual pytest argv tokens, for example the test files to run. Pytest suites only; passed as decoded argv, never a shell string.

requirements.description: Requirements files, relative to the suite path, installed into the suite's virtual environment when the acceptance image is built. Pytest suites only.

bindings.description: Environment variables the suite reads, each bound to a symbol from the closed source vocabulary -- never to an environment value. Resolution precedence per variable: explicit process environment (verbatim) -> source resolution -> declared default. template sources render last.

keyVaultBindings.description: Environment variable to Key Vault secret NAME, resolved from the stack's vault at run time. Secret values never appear in the descriptor.

loads.description: Named data loads the environment must have seeded (checked against published load facts by the deploy gate).

groups.description: Entitlement groups the test caller must hold.

dependencies.description: Sibling services this suite calls; a pinned dependency blocks the deploy gate with a typed reason.

forwards.description: In-cluster services the suite reaches directly. The lane opens a port-forward to the target the stack publishes under forwards in spi info --json and runs the suite with host networking, so the service answers on localhost at its published port. Bind forward:<target>:host and forward:<target>:port rather than static values so a caller running the suite elsewhere can point it at the forward. Maven suites only: the forwarded CA reaches the suite through a JVM trust store.
